_comment: Pinned on purpose (ported from ClawDeck's assets/versions.json, same author): everything is downloaded from its upstream at the moment the user asks, checked by sha256; GameCove ships none of these files.

xess_xmx_linux.sha256_note: xess-xmx-linux-20261104.zip (16508598 bytes), downloaded twice on 2026-11-09 with the same hash; its install.sh, uninstall.sh, enable.sh, disable.sh, xmx-launch.sh and LICENSE are byte-identical to the repo at tag 20261104 (a12948e2)
xess_xmx_linux.note: 20261104: low latency with XeSS frame generation on by default (IGDEXT_XELL_CAP), FSR 3.1+ games on XeSS (FSR=xess), XESS_FG up to 8x

reframework.note: Capcom RE Engine games: dinput8.dll (23252480 bytes, REFramework 0.1.0.69) next to the game's exe. onehoon's fork (the fork's author), release 15 built 2026-10-22, whose notes say to use it with OptiScaler in Capcom games: a working Windows Onimusha install runs exactly this file, and it booted and played with optiscaler_v10 on a Claw 8 EX on Bazzite (2026-11-04). Replaces praydog's nightly 01433: ClawDeck installs REFramework only together with the Capcom OptiScaler setup, and the fork is the build that setup was tested with. Releases 16 and 17 exist; not tested yet.

optiscaler.note: ClawDeck's own OptiScaler (optiscaler.py): the same release and OptiPatcher build Decky Framegen v0.17 pins, with the same sha256.

optiscaler_v10.note: Capcom RE Engine games only (optiscaler.py layout 'subfolder'): OptiScaler.dll as the proxy and OptiScaler.ini next to the exe, everything else in OptiScaler\ (OptiDllPath), OptiPatcher in OptiScaler\plugins. a working Windows Onimusha install uses 0.9.5-pre4, which isn't published on GitHub; this public v10 nightly ran Onimusha with onehoon's REFramework on a Claw 8 EX on Bazzite (2026-11-04). Every other game stays on 'optiscaler' (0.9.4). fakenvapi v1.4.1 (FakeMichau) goes in OptiScaler\ with the tested fakenvapi.ini, as in the tested folder: its fakenvapi.dll (415232 bytes) is byte-identical to the one OptiScaler 0.9.4 ships. OptiScaler v10 has fakenvapi built in ([fakenvapi] UseFakenvapi, set to true) and doesn't load the file; it is there to match the setup tested on the Claw.

fsr4_xmx.note: nitec's FSR 4.1.2 build for the XMX cores (OptiScaler community), shared with ClawDeck with nitec's OK (maintainer, 2026-11-05), the same files the tested setup installs on Intel (its Archives/Custom/FSR4_XMX). Hosted on ClawDeck's fsr4-xmx-files branch, pinned by commit (not on the Releases page); downloaded into ~/fsr4-xmx when missing, each sha256 checked (the maintainer's working copy on the Claw 8 EX, 2026-11-04).

fsr4_amd.license: AMD FidelityFX SDK binary licence (Kits/FidelityFX/docs/license.md): binary redistribution allowed with its notice; GameCove downloads it from AMD at the user's request instead of shipping it
fsr4_amd.note: AMD FSR SDK 2.4.0 (2026-10-28): FSR Upscaling 4.1.2, ML model picked by GPU (FP8 RDNA4, INT8 RDNA3/RDNA2 dGPU and Strix Halo, lightweight INT8 for Z2 Extreme / 890M / Z2 A). The same file ClawDeck keeps as fsr-original.dll next to nitec's XMX build. Under Proton FSR 4 needs a Proton with AMD's driver extension shim (Proton-CachyOS, GE-Proton).
